p: After falling consistently (1) _____ the U.S. dollar for a major part of the year, the rupee has (2) _____ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5% from its lowest levels (3) _____ in October. Even with this recent improvement, the rupee is still down about 11% since the start of the year. The rupee's performance has been closely (4) _____ to global crude oil prices. This makes sense, as imported oil accounts for about 80% of India's total demand. The value of the rupee dropped when oil prices climbed earlier this year, a trend that lasted until early October. Since then, as global crude prices have fallen, the rupee has (5) _____ against the dollar.

t: What should come in blank (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "After falling consistently (1) _____ the U.S. dollar..." (डॉलर के मुकाबले रुपये के लगातार गिरने की बात है; मुद्रा की तुलना में 'against' का प्रयोग होता है)। Hindi Meaning: के मुकाबले / के विरुद्ध.

t: What should come in blank (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "...the rupee has (2) _____ somewhat over the last few weeks. It has risen by almost 5%..." (गिरावट के बाद 5% की बढ़त बताई गई है, इसलिए रुपया कुछ हद तक 'उबरा / संभला' (recovered))। Hindi Meaning: उबरना / सुधरना.

t: What should come in blank (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "...from its lowest levels (3) _____ in October." (अक्टूबर में रुपया अपने न्यूनतम स्तर पर 'पहुँचा' (reached) था; स्तर को छूने के लिए reached उपयुक्त है)। Hindi Meaning: पहुँचना.

t: What should come in blank (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "The rupee's performance has been closely (4) _____ to global crude oil prices." (रुपये का प्रदर्शन कच्चे तेल की कीमतों से सीधे 'जुड़ा हुआ' है; closely tied to = निकट रूप से जुड़ा)। Hindi Meaning: जुड़ा हुआ / संबद्ध.

t: What should come in blank (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "...the rupee has (5) _____ against the dollar." (कच्चे तेल के दाम गिरने से रुपये की कीमत बढ़ी, यानी रुपया डॉलर के मुकाबले 'मजबूत हुआ' (strengthened))। Hindi Meaning: मजबूत होना.

p: To conceive of gender as ontologically prior or naturally originary is to misrecognize its status as a [1] _____, a semiotic and performative topology whose coherence is secured only through its reiteration across spatial, legal, and psychic apparatuses. Within this regime, embodiment is not merely lived but mediated-filtered through hermeneutic technologies that valorize some corporealities while rendering others abject, deviant, or structurally unintelligible. The state, in tandem with biomedical epistemes and juridico-political grammars, exercises a necropolitical calibration of life itself-where recognition is not a right but a [2] _____ allocated via matrices of intelligibility that are historically contingent and politically fungible. This dispositif renders gender a function of discursive legibility rather than biological inevitability. Resistance, when funneled through these grammars, risks becoming complicit in the very structures it seeks to subvert. Hence, the radical task is not merely to "expand" recognition but to effect a [3] _____ of recognition's ontological architecture. This entails refusing the dialectics of inclusion and exclusion that liberal frameworks offer and instead exposing their constitutive foreclosure of alterity. Such a politics necessitates the [4] _____ of normativity as a structuring logic of embodiment. Only through its unmaking can a post-identitarian ethics of becoming be envisioned-one that privileges contingency over coherence, opacity over transparency, and relational indeterminacy over categorical fixity. In this schema, freedom is not recuperative but [5] _____ -a rupture from taxonomic legibility, a departure from the logocentric compulsion to be known.

t: What should come in the place of blank number [1]?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: समाजशास्त्र में जेंडर (Gender) को एक स्थिर सच्चाई (naturally originary) नहीं, बल्कि एक "praxis-field" (व्यवहार या कर्म का क्षेत्र) माना जाता है, जहाँ चीज़ें समाज के रोज़मर्रा के नियमों और 'performance' से तय होती हैं। Hindi Meaning: व्यवहार का क्षेत्र (जहाँ काम/प्रदर्शन से चीज़ें तय हों).

t: What should come in the place of blank number [2]?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "recognition is not a right but a _____ allocated via matrices..." (समाज में मान्यता मिलना कोई जन्मसिद्ध अधिकार नहीं है, बल्कि यह एक "शर्त" है जो सिस्टम तय करता है)। 'Conditionality' का मतलब होता है 'सशर्तता' (कोई चीज़ जो शर्तों पर निर्भर हो)। Hindi Meaning: सशर्तता / शर्तों पर निर्भर होने की अवस्था.

t: What should come in the place of blank number [3]?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लेखक कह रहा है कि हमें इस सिस्टम को सिर्फ 'expand' (बढ़ाना) नहीं करना है, बल्कि इसके पूरे आर्किटेक्चर को 'ध्वस्त' करना है। दर्शन में ढाँचे को पूरी तरह नकारने या उजाड़ने को "Destitution" (अभाव/विनाश) कहा जाता है। Hindi Meaning: उजाड़ना / नष्ट करना / अभाव.

t: What should come in the place of blank number [4]?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "necessitates the _____ of normativity... Only through its unmaking..." अगले ही वाक्य में 'unmaking' (नष्ट करना) लिखा है। 'Ablation' एक सर्जिकल/मेडिकल शब्द है जिसका अर्थ है किसी चीज़ को पूरी तरह से काट कर निकाल देना या नष्ट कर देना। Hindi Meaning: पूरी तरह से काट कर हटा देना / नष्ट करना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number [5]?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "freedom is not recuperative but _____ -a rupture from taxonomic legibility". 'Apophatic' (निषेधात्मक) एक फिलॉसफिकल शब्द है जिसका मतलब है किसी चीज़ को नकार कर (negation के ज़रिए) उसे समझना (जैसे ईश्वर का वर्णन यह बताकर करना कि वह क्या *नहीं* है)। यहाँ स्वतंत्रता सिस्टम से खुद को 'नकारने' (depart होने) में है। Hindi Meaning: निषेधात्मक (नकार कर सच्चाई खोजना).

p: In the contemporary epoch of algorithmic governance and hyper-networked economies, the discourse of agency has undergone a paradigmatic mutation. No longer anchored in traditional notions of volition or deliberation, subjectivity is increasingly (1)_____ by ambient infrastructures that anticipate, nudge, and pre-empt decision-making before cognition consolidates intention. In such a regime, autonomy becomes retroactive — a post-facto narrative stitched together by feedback loops of personalization, predictive modeling, and biometric calibration. The liberal ideal of the rational actor, so central to modern jurisprudence and economic theory, finds itself (2)_____ under the weight of distributed cognition, machinic interpellation, and environmental scripting. Agency, in this schema, is not exercised but programmed; it is neither given nor seized but orchestrated through micro-environmental cues and algorithmic affordances. The individual becomes less a sovereign self than a (3)_____ node in a probabilistic matrix of behavioral speculation. Within this ontological reconfiguration, resistance too undergoes a semiotic shift. Acts of refusal no longer manifest through overt defiance but through obfuscation, misalignment, and withdrawal from legibility. Yet even these gestures risk being (4)_____ by the very systems they attempt to subvert — recuperated as marketable deviance, branded subcultures, or managed dissent. If every deviation is eventually re-circulated as novelty, then the terrain of the political itself becomes (5)_____ — evacuated of antagonism and steeped in simulation.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मानव व्यवहार (subjectivity) अब खुद के कंट्रोल में नहीं है, बल्कि डिजिटल सिस्टम्स द्वारा उसकी 'मध्यस्थता' या 'फिल्टरिंग' (mediated) की जाती है। Hindi Meaning: मध्यस्थता की गई / के माध्यम से प्रभावित.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "finds itself _____ under the weight..." डिजिटल दुनिया के बोझ तले जो 'rational actor' (स्वतंत्र रूप से सोचने वाला इंसान) का विचार है, वह 'कमज़ोर या नष्ट' (undermined) हो रहा है। Hindi Meaning: कमज़ोर होना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: इंसान अब एक स्वतंत्र व्यक्ति नहीं, बल्कि इस सिस्टम का महज़ एक ऐसा हिस्सा है जिसे 'डेटा में बदल दिया गया है' (datafied node)।

t: What should come in the place of blank number (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज कहता है कि हमारा विरोध (resistance) भी इस सिस्टम द्वारा "recuperated as marketable deviance" (बाज़ार में बेचने लायक बना दिया जाता है)। जब विरोध को ही सिस्टम अपने फायदे के लिए 'अपना' ले, तो उसे "Co-opted" कहते हैं। Hindi Meaning: अपने पक्ष में मिला लेना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "...evacuated of antagonism and steeped in simulation." (जहाँ कोई असली लड़ाई न बचे और सिर्फ दिखावा रह जाए)। ऐसी राजनीति जिसमें केवल दिखावा हो, उसे "Performative" (दिखावटी) कहते हैं।

p: The thyroid gland, a small butterfly-shaped organ located at the base of the neck, plays an (1) indispensable role in regulating the body's metabolism, growth, and development. Despite its modest size, the thyroid (3) a profound influence through the secretion of hormones such as thyroxine (T4) and triiodothyronine (T3), which orchestrate cellular activities and energy expenditure. Disruptions in thyroid function can manifest as hypothyroidism, characterized by insufficient hormone production, or hyperthyroidism, resulting from excessive secretion. Both conditions precipitate a spectrum of clinical symptoms ranging from fatigue, weight fluctuations, and cognitive impairment to more severe complications including cardiovascular anomalies and osteoporosis. The (2) aetiology of thyroid disorders is multifactorial, involving autoimmune mechanisms, iodine deficiency, genetic predisposition, and environmental factors. Diagnosis typically involves measuring serum levels of thyroid (4) hormones and thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH), supplemented by imaging modalities like ultrasound to evaluate gland morphology. Treatment strategies are tailored to the specific disorder, with hormone replacement therapy being the cornerstone for hypothyroidism, whereas antithyroid medications, radioactive iodine, or surgery may be employed for hyperthyroidism. Given the thyroid's pivotal role, maintaining its health is crucial. Public awareness campaigns emphasize adequate iodine intake and regular screening, especially in at-risk populations such as pregnant women and the elderly. Advancements (5) molecular biology and endocrinology continue to enhance our understanding, promising improved diagnostics and personalized therapeutic approaches in thyroid medicine.

t: The word "indispensable" in the passage most nearly means: (1)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Indispensable' का अर्थ होता है परम आवश्यक या जिसके बिना काम न चल सके। थायरॉयड शरीर के लिए बहुत ही 'ज़रूरी' (Essential) है। Hindi Meaning: अपरिहार्य / परम आवश्यक.

t: The word "aetiology" in the passage most nearly means: (2)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मेडिकल साइंस में 'Aetiology' (या Etiology) का मतलब होता है किसी बीमारी का कारण (Cause) या उसकी उत्पत्ति (Origin)। पैसेज में आगे बीमारी के कारण (आयोडीन की कमी, जेनेटिक्स) बताए गए हैं। Hindi Meaning: रोग का कारण.

t: Choose the appropriate verb to complete the sentence: (3)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य का Subject "the thyroid" (एकवचन) है। चूँकि बात एक वैज्ञानिक तथ्य (Present tense) की हो रही है, इसलिए Singular Subject के साथ Singular Verb (V1+s/es) यानी 'Exerts' (प्रभाव डालता है) का प्रयोग होगा। Hindi Meaning: (प्रभाव) डालता है.

t: Find out the part of speech of the word: (4)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "thyroid hormones" में 'thyroid' यह बता रहा है कि हॉर्मोन किस प्रकार का है (Adjective का काम कर रहा है), जबकि 'hormones' मुख्य संज्ञा (Noun) है जो शरीर के रसायनों का नाम है।

t: Choose the correct preposition: (5)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जब भी हम किसी विषय या विज्ञान के क्षेत्र (Field of study) में प्रगति या विकास (Advancements) की बात करते हैं, तो Preposition 'in' का इस्तेमाल होता है (जैसे: Advancements in technology / Advancements in biology)।

p: Electric vehicles (EVs) promise lower emissions, quieter cities, and reduced dependence on fossil fuels. However, the transition to electric mobility requires substantial investment in charging infrastructure, reliable electricity grids, and sustainable battery production. (A) _____, policymakers must recognize that technological innovation alone cannot guarantee widespread adoption. Consumer confidence depends on affordability, charging availability, battery longevity, and transparent regulatory standards. Although EVs reduce tailpipe emissions, irresponsible mining practices may (B) _____ ecological degradation in resource-rich regions if environmental safeguards remain inadequate. Governments, industries, and research institutions must therefore develop cleaner extraction techniques and promote battery recycling and alternative materials. If governments (C) _____ clear and consistent policy incentives, consumers would feel more confident about investing in electric vehicles despite their higher initial costs. Such confidence may encourage manufacturers to expand production and reduce prices. Equally important is the creation of an (D) _____ that rewards innovation without discouraging fair competition. Long-term industrial growth also depends on institutional credibility and predictable governance. Ultimately, the success of electric mobility will be determined by society's willingness to invest (E) _____ a comprehensive transition that balances environmental responsibility, economic practicality, and social equity.

t: Identify the correct discourse marker for blank (A).
q.e: The sentence introduces a logical conclusion drawn from the preceding context, which highlights that transitioning requires substantial investment. "Therefore" is the appropriate conjunctive adverb used to show a consequence or result based on the evidence presented.

t: Identify the correct word for blank (B).
q.e: The verb "exacerbate" means to make a bad situation or problem worse. In the context of irresponsible mining practices causing further environmental harm, "exacerbate" is the most logically and contextually appropriate choice.

t: Identify the correct word/phrase for blank (C).
q.e: The sentence follows the structure of a second conditional, which uses the simple past tense in the 'if'-clause to describe a hypothetical condition ("If governments provided...") leading to a probable result in the main clause ("consumers would feel more confident").

t: Identify the correct phrase for blank (D).
q.e: The context discusses establishing a comprehensive, balanced environment that nurtures innovation while maintaining fair competition. "Economic ecosystem" accurately refers to an interconnected network of policies, businesses, and institutions working together, making it the most suitable phrase to complete the sentence meaningfully.

t: Identify the correct preposition for blank (E).
q.e: The verb "invest" is idiomatically followed by the preposition "in" when indicating the object or initiative receiving the allocated resources or effort ("invest in a comprehensive transition"). Therefore, the preposition "in" is grammatically correct and best completes the blank.

p: Sustainable farming is meant to satisfy current needs without hurting the potential of future generations to supply food. This method focuses on practices that reduce environmental degradation while sustaining productivity. One of its main principles is (1) where crops are rotated to maintain soil quality and prevent the necessity of chemical fertilizers. Another key feature is water management. Effective irrigation systems can avert waste and make sure that water resources are responsibly used. Farmers also use (2) practices, e.g., planting cover crops, to avert erosion and preserve biodiversity.

Sustainable agriculture is not solely concerned with environmental yields; it also supports economic and social objectives. By minimising dependency on costly inputs, farmers can save money and enhance their (3) _. Furthermore, encouraging equitable labour practices means that employees are treated fairly and paid accordingly.

t: While it has its perks, sustainable agriculture has its drawbacks too, such as resistance to innovation and a lack of resources. To overcome these obstacles, governments, organisations, and (4) must work together. By adopting sustainable practices, we can create a food system that is robust and (5)
What should come in the place of blank number 1?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The text immediately defines the principle: "where crops are rotated to maintain soil quality." This is the exact definition of "Crop rotation," providing a clear contextual clue. Hindi Meaning: फसल चक्र.

t: While it has its perks, sustainable agriculture has its drawbacks too, such as resistance to innovation and a lack of resources. To overcome these obstacles, governments, organisations, and (4) must work together. By adopting sustainable practices, we can create a food system that is robust and (5)
What should come in the place of blank number 2?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: Practices like planting cover crops to avert erosion and preserve biodiversity fall under "Conservation" practices, which are actions aimed at protecting and preserving natural resources. Hindi Meaning: संरक्षण.

t: While it has its perks, sustainable agriculture has its drawbacks too, such as resistance to innovation and a lack of resources. To overcome these obstacles, governments, organisations, and (4) must work together. By adopting sustainable practices, we can create a food system that is robust and (5)
What should come in the place of blank number 3?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The passage shifts to discussing "economic and social objectives." "Saving money" by minimizing "costly inputs" directly enhances a farmer's financial "Profits." Hindi Meaning: मुनाफा / लाभ.

t: While it has its perks, sustainable agriculture has its drawbacks too, such as resistance to innovation and a lack of resources. To overcome these obstacles, governments, organisations, and (4) must work together. By adopting sustainable practices, we can create a food system that is robust and (5)
What should come in the place of blank number 4?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The sentence lists "governments, organisations, and ___". To complete this triad encompassing all levels of society, "Individuals" (everyday citizens) is the most logical choice. Hindi Meaning: व्यक्ति / आम लोग.

t: While it has its perks, sustainable agriculture has its drawbacks too, such as resistance to innovation and a lack of resources. To overcome these obstacles, governments, organisations, and (4) must work together. By adopting sustainable practices, we can create a food system that is robust and (5)
What should come in the place of blank number 5?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The conjunction "and" connects two adjectives with similar positive connotations. "Robust" means strong and sturdy. "Resilient" (able to withstand or recover quickly from difficult conditions) is the perfect companion word. Hindi Meaning: लचीला (जो मुश्किलों से जल्दी उबर सके ).

p: The master-slave dialectic exemplifies this: self-consciousness seeks recognition from another, yet in asserting its dominance over the other, it paradoxically (3) _____ its own freedom.

q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य एक सार्वकालिक दार्शनिक विचार बता रहा है और बाक़ी verbs ("seeks", "exemplifies") Present tense में हैं। Subject singular है, इसलिए singular present verb "undermines" चाहिए। अर्थ भी फ़िट होता है: दूसरे पर हावी होना विरोधाभासी रूप से अपनी ही सच्ची आज़ादी को कमज़ोर करता है। उत्तर (a) undermines। Hindi Meaning: कमज़ोर करना।

p: The architecture of modern policymaking increasingly reflects a shift from dialogic consensus to technocratic unilateralism. Public consultation, once a hallmark of democratic ethos, is now frequently (1) ___ by algorithmic forecasting and data-driven mandates. While such models brag precision, they risk sustaining systemic (2) ___ by embedding pre-existing prejudices into ostensibly neutral code. This evolution is further complicated by the political spectacle, where performative symbolism often supplants substantive reform. Leaders indulge in rhetorical grandstanding, constructing narratives that are (3) ___ rather than transformative. Consequently, public trust erodes, not due to apathy but from acute

(4) ___ - a recognition that participation no longer guarantees influence. To reclaim legitimacy, institutions must reimagine governance not as a procedural mechanism but as an iterative, dialogical act. This demands epistemic humility, the willingness to engage multiple worldviews without defaulting to technocratic (5) ___. Only then can policy transcend compliance and cultivate authentic democratic agency.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 1?
q.sr: [SSC Stenographer Grade C & D Examination, 2026, 15 sep 2026, Shift-1]
q.e: The text aggressively laments that traditional public consultation is heavily being replaced by emotionless machine algorithms. "Superseded" is the perfectly accurate formal term meaning to rapidly take the place of a person or thing previously in authority.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 2?
q.e: The passage immediately defines the problem as "embedding pre-existing prejudices" directly into computer systems. Therefore, the term "biases", which acts as an exact synonym for deep-seated unfair prejudice or massive favoritism, is the unequivocally correct contextual choice.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 3?
q.e: The sentence fiercely contrasts political narratives with being genuinely "transformative". If the narrative totally lacks substantive real-world reform and is purely a performative spectacle, then it is merely "Ornamental" (serving only to decorate or distract without utility).

t: What should come in the place of blank number 4?
q.e: The passage vividly describes citizens violently losing deep-seated public trust because they realize their active participation is now totally meaningless. This massive feeling of bitter disappointment upon discovering an institution is hollow is perfectly defined as "Disillusionment".

t: What should come in the place of blank number 5?
q.e: The author demands "epistemic humility" and an open willingness to genuinely engage multiple differing worldviews. The exact psychological antonym to this humility and openness is "Dogmatism"—the highly arrogant assertion of strict technical rules as absolute, undeniable truths.

p: In contemporary cognitive science, human judgment is increasingly understood as a product of layered neural and psychological mechanisms rather than a purely rational calculus. Decisions that appear deliberate are often (A) ___ by unconscious biases that subtly recalibrate perception before conscious deliberation even begins. This recognition has significantly undermined earlier models of rational agency, suggesting instead that cognition is dynamically constructed in real time. Within this framework, behavioural economists argue that heuristics, while computationally efficient, can (B) ___ systematic errors in probabilistic reasoning, particularly under conditions of uncertainty and informational overload. Such errors are not incidental but structurally embedded within the architecture of human cognition. Clinical psychology has similarly evolved, with therapeutic paradigms increasingly encouraging individuals to (C) ___ entrenched cognitive schemas rather than merely suppressing symptomatic expressions of distress. This shift reflects an understanding that maladaptive thought patterns are self-reinforcing and resistant to superficial correction. Neuroscientific evidence further indicates that the brain (D) ___ capable of extensive functional reorganization, even in adulthood, thereby challenging earlier assumptions about fixed neural circuitry. This adaptability underpins many modern rehabilitative and psychotherapeutic interventions. Nevertheless, scholars caution that public discourse often (E) ___ complex psychological constructs into overly simplistic explanatory frames, thereby obscuring the nuanced interplay between cognition, emotion, and environment.

t: Fill in the blank (A) with the correct word:
q.e: "Mediated" means brought about, influenced, or shaped through an intervening medium or agency. In this context, decisions are influenced and shaped by unconscious biases before conscious deliberation begins, making "mediated" the most precise and contextually appropriate choice.

t: Fill in the blank (B) with the correct word:
q.e: "Engender" means to cause, produce, or give rise to a feeling, situation, or condition. In the passage, behavioral economists argue that heuristic shortcuts can give rise to or produce systematic errors in probabilistic reasoning, making "engender" the correct answer.

t: Fill in the blank (C) with the correct word.
q.e: "Deconstruct" means to critically examine and break down complex concepts or structures into constituent elements. In therapy, the objective is to dismantle deeply ingrained, maladaptive cognitive patterns rather than reinforce them, making "deconstruct" the most contextually appropriate verb.

t: Fill in the blank (D) with the correct word.
q.e: The linking verb "remains" properly denotes an ongoing, enduring state of being. Combined with the predicate adjective "capable," it indicates that the brain continues to preserve its adaptive neuroplastic capacity throughout adult life, contradicting outdated static models.

p: The increasing rate of substance abuse among the youth has been recognized as a major public health issue in contemporary society, which affects not only the concerned youth but also the stability of the community as a whole. p: Swimming is one of the most popular recreational and competitive activities worldwide, valued for both its fitness benefits and its ability to provide relaxation. Unlike many forms of exercise, swimming is (1) low-impact, making it ideal for people of all ages and fitness levels. Knowing how to swim can be (2) "life-saving" in emergencies and helps individuals enjoy other water-based activities such as boating, diving, and surfing. Competitive swimming, on the other hand, demands rigorous training, discipline, and excellent technique. Different strokes freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, and butterfly engage various muscle groups and require distinct breathing patterns. Regular swimming improves cardiovascular health, increases lung capacity, and promotes overall well-being. It's also an effective way to reduce stress, as the rhythmic movements and sensation of being in water can have a calming effect on the mind. However, safety is crucial. p: Quantum computing exploits subatomic phenomena to perform calculations beyond conventional computers' capabilities. Entanglement allows qubits to be instantly linked, so measuring one instantly tells you about its partner's state regardless of distance. But practical challenges remain significant. Qubits are (1) _____ to environmental noise, causing "decoherence" that destroys computation. Error rates are (2) _____, making fault-tolerant quantum computing still elusive. p: The pursuit of global equity in the anthropocene is less a matter of distributive justice and more a theatre of ontological misrecognition. While the Global North presents technocratic solutions as universally applicable, such solutions often encode assumptions of temporal supremacy and civilizational [1] _____. Climate finance, for instance, masquerades as benevolence while entrenching hierarchies of surveillance and dependence. The epistemes of the South, rather than being engaged on their own terms, are often reconfigured through extractive logics of "capacity building," a term whose etymology betrays its colonial [2] _____. Embedded within these discourses is the idea that certain populations must be "readied" for modernity-thus reproducing a pedagogical asymmetry that masks itself as aid. Meanwhile, planetary imaginaries are increasingly framed through cartographies of emergency. The language of "tipping points" and "irreversible loss" evokes a moral urgency that, paradoxically, facilitates a form of ecological [3] _____, wherein radical structural reform is substituted by incremental techno-fixes. Carbon offsets, biodiversity credits, and green financialization proliferate not as correctives, but as symptoms of an underlying refusal to dislodge anthropocentric capitalism. In such a milieu, protest is not silence-breaking but often met with strategic [4] _____, where rhetorical accommodation obscures institutional inertia. Civil society is co-opted, not crushed. The subaltern voice is archived, not amplified. Thus, to reclaim ecological justice is not merely to demand inclusion, but to interrogate the ontologies that define inclusion itself. Absent this, the dream of planetary stewardship will remain a ceremonial [5] _____, rich in symbolism, barren in substance.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (4)?

In such structures, the auxiliary verb "will" must come before the subject "users." Therefore, "will users begin" is the only grammatically correct arrangement.

p: Organ donation is a remarkable act of (4) altruism that can save countless lives. Innovations like artificial organs and regenerative medicine offer hope for reducing dependency on donors, but these technologies are still in (5) nascent stages. p: India's push to expand semiconductor manufacturing has generated optimism, but factories alone will not guarantee success. t: What should come in the place of blank number (4)?

p: In the archipelago of epistemic fracture, where coherence is a relic and continuity a performative illusion, cognition unfolds not through linear causality but via stochastic pulses of informational detritus. Within this disjunctive matrix, agency is less a property of autonomous will than a side effect of algorithmic interpellation. Every action is (1)_____ not as a result of volition but as an emergent behavior — calculated, inferred, and subtly modulated by systems of predictive design. Identity, in this terrain, ceases to be ontological and becomes computational: a fluid sequence of statistical probabilities encoded and re-encoded through bio-digital feedback loops. The notion of authorship is retrofitted, no longer a site of expression but a (2)_____ node in a decentralized economy of semiotic production. Language, once the principal vessel of intentionality, now functions as a carrier signal for behavioral cues — optimized not for meaning but for engagement velocity. In this regime, dissent is not censored but (3)_____ — subtly realigned to serve the centripetal logics of monetized attention. The archive is not a memory but a battleground: past and present re-stitched according to the dictates of data retention, compliance heuristics, and platformed ontology. What remains is not truth but latency: the delay between perception and its (4)_____ by computational governance. p: In the modern digital age, the shift toward algorithmic governance suggests a world where human bias is replaced by the cold, mathematical precision of code. From credit scoring to judicial sentencing, automated systems are being integrated into the very fabric of institutional decision-making. The promise is one of efficiency and radical neutrality, (A)_______ away the subjective whims of human administrators. However, this perceived neutrality is often illusory; algorithms are, after all, trained on historical data that inevitably (B)_______ the prejudices of the past. If the training data contains systemic biases against certain demographics, the machine learns those patterns as "truths". Far from eliminating discrimination, the algorithm may simply hide it behind a veneer of technical objectivity. Should a predictive policing system be designed to identify high-risk neighbourhoods, it might inadvertently codify and amplify existing systemic inequalities. By targeting areas that were already over-policed due to historical bias, the system creates a feedback loop. The "math" then appears to justify the (C)_______ targeting of those same communities, creating a cycle that is difficult to break. (D)_______ these tools offer undeniable efficiency in processing vast amounts of data, they lack the "moral imagination" required for true justice. Amachine can identify a statistical correlation, but it cannot understand the nuance of human circumstance or the socio-economic context behind a data point. It treats humans as static variables rather than evolving individuals. This creates a dangerous (E)_______ where the pursuit of objective fairness results in the automated replication of historical harm. As we outsource our judgement to software, we risk losing the ability to hold systems accountable. We must ensure that the drive for technological progress does not come at the expense of the very equity we seek to achieve.

Meanwhile, epistemic asymmetries persist: indigenous knowledge is (4) _____ as "local insight," offered just enough space to decorate, never to reorient. Environmental justice, once confrontational, now wears a diplomatic smile, folded neatly into intergovernmental communiqués. p: Nestled in the serene mountains of Japan lies a quaint and captivating locale famously known as the Doll Village. p: Contemporary governance will typically disguise itself in terms of agility and crisis response. From climate early warning systems to pandemic dashboards, there is a rapidly increasing apparatus that promises the vision of being in control. Such aids, while useful, tend to (1) ___ the public eye away from structural disparities by concentrating on short-term metrics. What looks like responsiveness tends to be mere reactivity in a system that is optimized for optics, not results. Governments implement short-term programs, presented as "emergency relief," but too frequently without vision or representation in the long term. p: The human brain’s ability to rewire itself, a phenomenon known as neuroplasticity, is most evident during early childhood development. This period of high "synaptic pruning" allows the brain to specialise, based on the specific stimuli it receives from the environment. It is the reason children can learn multiple languages with an ease that adults often find (A)_______. It is during this "critical period" that children internalise the complex, underlying rules of abstract syntax without any formal instruction. They don't just mimic sounds; they (B)_______ the deep structural logic of their native tongue. This innate capacity for grammar suggests that the human mind is biologically "pre-wired" for linguistic complexity. If a child were deprived of linguistic input during these formative years, the window for achieving native-level fluency might close forever. Cases of "feral children" have shown that (C)_______ vocabulary can be acquired later in life, the subtle mastery of syntax—the ability to weave thoughts into complex structures—is almost impossible to recover once the critical window shuts. Since neuroplasticity continues into adulthood, it does so at a significantly diminished rate. The adult brain is more stable and less "malleable", which is beneficial for maintaining long-term memories but detrimental for the rapid acquisition of entirely new systems of thought. Learning a language at forty is a cognitive (D)_______; at four, it is an effortless absorption. This biological constraint highlights the (E)_______ nature of language acquisition, where timing is as critical as the stimulus itself. It serves as a reminder that our cognitive architecture is not just a product of our will but a reflection of a strictly timed biological schedule. To master the mind, one must first understand the clock by which it grows.

t: Which word best completes blank (A) to describe the level of ease with which children learn languages, as viewed by adults?
q.e: The word "enviable" is an adjective meaning "highly desirable" or "likely to excite envy." In the context of the passage, adults find the ease with which children learn languages to be a desirable quality that they themselves lack, making "enviable" the most appropriate choice.

q.e: The passage describes a general biological fact about how children process language. The simple present tense "deduce" is used to state habitual actions or general truths. Since the sentence discusses an innate capacity that children possess generally, the base form "deduce" fits the grammatical structure perfectly.

t: Which conjunction best completes blank (C) to establish the contrast between the ability to learn vocabulary and the inability to master syntax later in life?
q.e: The conjunction "while" is used to introduce a contrast between two simultaneous facts. Here, it contrasts the fact that vocabulary can be acquired later in life with the fact that subtle mastery of syntax is almost impossible to recover once the critical window shuts.

t: Which word best completes blank (D) to contrast the difficulty of adult language learning with the ease of childhood acquisition?
q.e: The passage contrasts the "effortless absorption" of a child with the significant difficulty faced by an adult. "Battle" metaphorically represents a hard struggle or a difficult task, which perfectly fits the context of adult cognitive effort

t: Which word best completes blank (E) to describe the critical,time-sensitive nature of language acquisition?
q.e: The word "pivotal" means of crucial importance in relation to the development or success of something else. In the context of a "biological constraint" and a "strictly timed biological schedule," the time-sensitive nature of language acquisition is indeed pivotal.

p: In recent years, bio-surveillance has migrated from the periphery of crisis management into the marrow of everyday governance. What began as a provisional response to epidemiological disruption has, with startling velocity, matured into a (1)_____ instrument of statecraft. The body, once a site of private experience, is now parsed into micro-indicators, archived not as narratives but as anomalies within statistical matrices. The threshold for intervention has shifted — not at diagnosis, but at deviation. Such a regime thrives on a curious inversion: surveillance no longer reacts to illness; it anticipates it. The calculus of care becomes indistinguishable from the logic of control, and protection is no longer offered but enforced. In this architecture, the citizen is both beneficiary and suspect, suspended in a biopolitical gaze that renders health a function of (2)_____, not autonomy. What is striking, however, is not merely the pervasiveness of this apparatus, but its opacity. Embedded technologies track pulse, breath, temperature — but who interprets? Who decides what qualifies as pathological? The grammar of governance here is not public but procedural, not deliberative but (3)_____. If unchecked, this mode risks normalizing a world in which vigilance masquerades as virtue. The ethical stakes are not peripheral but foundational: in rendering health as measurable, we risk rendering it (4)_____. The ineffable — pain, anxiety, even trust — becomes illegible within a model that privileges only what can be graphed. The challenge, then, is not to reject technology but to reinscribe its terms. Bio-surveillance must be subject to democratic scrutiny, not immune to it. Otherwise, we inherit not safety but a simulated solidarity, and in its name, a deeply (5)_____ submission.

p: Passage: The spread of digital payments has made daily transactions faster, but convenience can also breed (1) _____. Fraudsters rely less on technical brilliance and more on human (2) _____, persuading users to reveal confidential details. Banks therefore advise customers to verify links, avoid hurried decisions and treat every unsolicited request with (3) _____. Public awareness campaigns are useful, yet their effect remains limited unless users develop a (4) _____ habit of checking sources. In the digital economy, trust is valuable, but blind trust can be financially (5) _____.

t: Choose the most suitable word for blank (1).
q.e: In the context of digital payments, "convenience" often leads people to become less careful or overly relaxed about security. "Complacency" perfectly describes this state of uncritical satisfaction with oneself or one's security, which fraudsters then exploit to their advantage in financial scams.

t: Choose the most suitable word for blank (2).
q.e: The passage states that fraudsters persuade users to reveal confidential details. This relies on "credulity," which is a tendency to be too ready to believe that something is real or true. It fits the context of being easily deceived by scammers through manipulation.

t: Choose the most suitable word for blank (3).
q.e: The context of the passage focuses on security and avoiding fraud. Banks advise customers to be cautious; therefore, treating unsolicited requests with "suspicion" is the logical choice to prevent falling victim to scams. Other options like "gratitude" or "enthusiasm" are inappropriate for security warnings.

t: Choose the most suitable word for blank (4).
q.e: The passage suggests that for awareness campaigns to be effective, users must make checking sources a regular part of their routine. "Habitual" correctly describes a behavior that is done regularly and repeatedly, which is necessary for maintaining long-term digital security and safety.

t: Choose the most suitable word for blank (5).
q.e: The sentence warns about the dangers of "blind trust" in the digital economy. Such trust can lead to devastating financial consequences or total loss, making "ruinous" the most fitting adjective. It emphasizes the severe negative impact that lack of caution can have.

p: Literature, far from being a static repository of aesthetic delight, is a restless medium through which cultures interrogate themselves. The novel, the poem, the play-all are not merely forms but fields wherein ideologies (1) _____, mutate, and sometimes dissolve. To read deeply is to risk disorientation, for every interpretation implies an act of displacement: of authorial intent, of reader expectation, of historical certainty. The literary canon itself is less a monument than a (2) _____-a site of contestation shaped by inclusion, exclusion, and reinvention. A Shakespearean soliloquy may bear universal resonance, yet it also emerges from a matrix of Elizabethan anxieties and power structures. The illusion of timelessness is, more often than not, a function of critical emphasis rather than intrinsic merit. Postcolonial and feminist critiques have challenged this apparent neutrality, foregrounding the voices that were once peripheral. Such interventions have not diminished literature's prestige but instead (3) _____ its moral and political stakes. Texts once considered apolitical are now read as cultural artifacts entangled in empire, patriarchy, and resistance. In this light, literary criticism becomes an act not of judgment but of (4) _____-an excavation of silences as much as meanings. The reader, then, is not a passive consumer but a co-creator, whose insights must be (5) _____ with humility and historical awareness.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (1)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "mutate, and sometimes dissolve" (बदलना और कभी-कभी खत्म हो जाना)। यह एक बहुत ही उग्र (turbulent) माहौल है। इस मैदान (fields) में विचारधाराएं (ideologies) आपस में "टकराती" (collide) हैं, बदलती हैं और खत्म होती हैं। Hindi Meaning: टकराना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (2)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: डैश (-) के ठीक बाद उस शब्द को परिभाषित किया गया है: "a site of contestation" (विवाद या संघर्ष की जगह)। साहित्य का कैनन कोई शांत स्मारक नहीं, बल्कि एक "युद्ध का मैदान (battleground)" है जहाँ अलग-अलग विचार लड़ते हैं। Hindi Meaning: युद्ध का मैदान.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (3)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "have not diminished... but instead..." (घटाया नहीं है... बल्कि इसके बजाय...)। यहाँ 'diminish' (कम करना) का विलोम शब्द चाहिए। 'Intensified' (तीव्र करना या बढ़ाना) इस कॉन्ट्रास्ट (विरोध) को पूरा करता है। Hindi Meaning: तीव्र कर दिया / बढ़ा दिया.

t: What should come in the place of blank number (4)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: डैश (-) के ठीक बाद लिखा है: "an excavation of silences" (चुप्पियों की खुदाई)। इतिहास और अर्थ की गहरी परतों की 'खुदाई' (excavation) करने का काम "पुरातत्व (archaeology)" से जुड़ता है। यहाँ साहित्यिक आलोचना को एक प्रकार की आर्केलॉजी बताया गया है। Hindi Meaning: पुरातत्व (गहरी खुदाई करके खोजना).

t: What should come in the place of blank number (5)?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पाठक के विचार (insights) सिर्फ आक्रामक नहीं होने चाहिए, बल्कि वे विनम्रता (humility) और ऐतिहासिक जागरूकता के साथ "संतुलित या नरम" (tempered) होने चाहिए। "Tempered with" एक बेहतरीन Collocation है। Hindi Meaning: संतुलित करना / संयमित करना.

p: In modern societies, the concept of freedom is often celebrated as an essential right. However, true freedom is not the absence of rules but the presence of thoughtful (1) _____. Without it, freedom risks turning into chaos, where individual actions undermine collective welfare. A society that prizes only personal liberty without shared responsibility may soon face moral and civic (2) _____. While people often equate freedom with doing as they please, meaningful liberty requires a commitment to boundaries that preserve dignity and (3) _____ for all. This balance is difficult to maintain, especially in democracies where voices are many and interests often (4) _____. Yet, it is precisely through dialogue, compromise, and mutual respect that freedom finds its most enduring expression. In the end, freedom divorced from responsibility is not progress, but a subtle (5) _____ of what it truly means to be free.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 1?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: असली आज़ादी नियमों का न होना नहीं है, बल्कि एक विचारशील "संयम" (Restraint) का होना है। 'Restraint' का अर्थ है खुद पर काबू रखना या सीमाओं में रहना। Hindi Meaning: संयम / नियंत्रण.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 2?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जो समाज बिना किसी ज़िम्मेदारी के केवल व्यक्तिगत आज़ादी को महत्व देता है, वह जल्द ही नैतिक और नागरिक "पतन या पतन" (Collapse) का सामना करे गा। 'Revival' (पुनर्जन्म) इसका विलोम है। Hindi Meaning: पतन / ढह जाना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 3?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "boundaries that preserve dignity and justice for all". गरिमा (dignity) के साथ सबसे अच्छा मेल खाने वाला शब्द 'न्याय' (justice) है। सच्ची आज़ादी का मतलब है कि सबके लिए गरिमा और न्याय सुनिश्चित किया जाए। Hindi Meaning: न्याय.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 4?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: लोकतंत्र में कई आवाज़ें होती हैं और अक्सर लोगों के हित आपस में "टकराते" (clash) हैं। 'Clash' का अर्थ है दो अलग-अलग विचारों या हितों का आमने-सामने टकराना। Hindi Meaning: टकराना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 5?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: बिना ज़िम्मेदारी के आज़ादी कोई प्रगति नहीं है, बल्कि यह आज़ादी के असली मतलब का एक "विरूपण या विकृति" (Distortion) है। यानी यह आज़ादी के सही अर्थ को तोड़-मरोड़ कर पेश करना है। Hindi Meaning: विकृति / तोड़-मरोड़.

p: Millets, a group of small-seeded grains, (3) ___ for thousands of years in India and other parts of Asia and Africa. Once considered the "poor man's food," they are now gaining recognition for their (1) nutritional value and environmental benefits. Rich in fibre, protein, vitamins, and minerals, millets are a powerhouse of health, aiding digestion, improving heart health, and helping regulate blood sugar levels. Unlike rice and wheat, millets require far less water to grow and can thrive in arid and semi-arid regions. This makes them not only a healthy choice but also a

(2) sustainable one, particularly important in the face of climate change and depleting water resources. There are (4) ___ varieties of millets, including finger millet (ragi), pearl millet (bajra), and foxtail millet, each with its unique taste and health benefits. These grains can be used in a wide range of dishes from traditional rotis and porridges to modern snacks and desserts. Despite their benefits, millets had fallen out of favour for decades due to changing food preferences and the dominance of rice and wheat in markets. However, with increasing health awareness (5) ___ government campaigns, they are making a comeback on urban menus and in packaged food products.

t: In the passage, what does "nutritional" most nearly mean?
o: Related to value of food for health
q.e: The term "nutritional" refers to the specific biochemical process of providing or obtaining the food necessary for sustaining physical health and vigorous growth. It directly relates to the intrinsic health value of the food consumed.

t: The word "sustainable" in the passage is closest in meaning to:
o: Able to be maintained over time without harm
q.e: In the fields of agriculture and ecology, "sustainable" denotes methods that strictly avoid the depletion of vital natural resources. It means practices can be continuously maintained over time without causing long-term harm to the environment.

t: Choose the correct auxiliary verb and main verb: (3)
q.e: The subject of the sentence, "Millets", is undeniably a plural noun. Because it represents a passive action occurring over thousands of years up to the present, the plural present perfect passive "have been cultivated" is required.

t: Choose the correct quantifier: (4)
q.e: The noun "varieties" is a countable plural noun. Quantifiers such as "much", "little", and "a large amount of" are strictly reserved for uncountable nouns. Therefore, "several" is the only grammatically acceptable option for countable plurals.

t: Choose the appropriate conjunction: (5)
q.e: The sentence lists two completely parallel, harmonious factors contributing to the comeback of millets: "increasing health awareness" alongside "government campaigns". The coordinating conjunction "and" is perfectly suited to elegantly connect these two cooperative noun phrases.

p: Medical expenses (3) a significant concern worldwide, impacting individuals and governments alike. In India, the cost of healthcare is generally lower compared to many Western countries, yet it still poses a substantial burden on a large portion of the population. India's healthcare system is a blend of public and private providers, with the private sector accounting for the majority of medical expenditure. Despite relatively affordable treatment costs, many Indians struggle to pay for quality healthcare due to inadequate insurance coverage and low per capita income. In contrast, countries like the United States and those in Western Europe have significantly higher medical expenses. The U.S., in particular, spends an enormous percentage of its GDP on healthcare, driven by advanced technology, high labor costs, and administrative expenses. While insurance coverage is more widespread, out-of-pocket expenses can still be very high, especially for those without

(4) plans. European countries with universal healthcare systems, such as the UK and Germany, manage to keep individual costs lower by funding healthcare through taxation. This model ensures wider access but often leads to longer wait times for (2) elective procedures. Medical expenses (5) to rise globally due to factors such as aging populations, increasing prevalence of chronic diseases, and rapid technological advancements. India faces the dual challenge of improving healthcare accessibility while controlling costs. Innovations like telemedicine and government initiatives aim to alleviate some financial pressures, but significant
(1) disparities remain.

t: Select the word that is the most appropriate antonym of "disparities" as used in the passage: (1)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: पैसेज में 'Disparities' (असमानताएं ) शब्द का इस्तेमाल हुआ है। इसका विलोम (Antonym) पूछा गया है। Disparities का अर्थ होता है बहुत बड़ा अंतर या भेदभाव (जैसे अमीर-गरीब में)। इसका सटीक उल्टा 'Uniformities' (समानताएं / एकरूपता) होगा। बाकी विकल्प (Inequalities, Differences, Variations) इसके समानार्थी (Synonyms) हैं। Hindi Meaning: असमानताएं (Disparities) -> समानताएं (Uniformities).

t: What does the term "elective procedures" refer to in the passage? (2)
o: Surgeries decided by the patient, not immediately necessary
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: मेडिकल साइंस में 'Elective procedures' (वैकल्पिक प्रक्रियाएं ) उन सर्जरी या इलाजों को कहते हैं जिन्हें मरीज़ या डॉक्टर पहले से तय करते हैं क्योंकि वे जानलेवा या इमरजेंसी नहीं होते (जैसे प्लास्टिक सर्जरी या मोतियाबिंद का ऑपरे शन)। Hindi Meaning: अपनी मर्ज़ी से चुनी गई, जो आपातकालीन न हो।

t: Choose the correct verb: (3)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में "impacting individuals..." का उपयोग हुआ है, जो दिखाता है कि कोई चीज़ जो पास्ट में शुरू हुई थी, वह आज भी सच है और असर डाल रही है। इसके लिए 'Present Perfect Tense' का इस्तेमाल होता है। Subject "Medical expenses" Plural (बहुवचन) है, इसलिए 'Have become' सही होगा। Grammar Rule: Plural Subject + Have + V3.

t: Choose the appropriate word: (4)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: वाक्य में 'plans' एक Noun (संज्ञा) है। Noun की विशेषता बताने के लिए हमें एक Adjective ( विशेषण) चाहिए। "Comprehensive" एक Adjective है जिसका मतलब होता है 'विस्तृत' या 'व्यापक' (जिसमें सब कुछ शामिल हो)। Hindi Meaning: व्यापक (सब कुछ कवर करने वाला).

t: Choose the correct verb form: (5)
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: यहाँ Subject "Medical expenses" (चिकित्सा व्यय) है, जो Plural (बहुवचन) है। Present Indefinite Tense के नियमानुसार, Plural Subject के साथ Verb की First Form (V1 बिना s/es के ) आती है। इसलिए 'Continue' सही जवाब है। Grammar Rule: Plural Subject -> Plural Verb (V1).

p: Good governance is essential for the stability and progress of any nation. It involves transparency, accountability, and effective delivery of public services. Policies must be designed not just for short-term gains but to ensure long-term development. A government that prioritizes public welfare must also be open to (1)______ and citizen feedback. However, even well-meaning policies can fail if poorly implemented. Coordination between departments and timely communication are (2)______ for achieving outcomes. Public awareness and access to accurate information also help in reducing (3)______ in governance. Digital platforms and e-governance tools have made it easier for citizens to track services, report grievances, and (4)______ participation. A responsive and inclusive government must constantly evaluate its policies to match the changing needs of society. Ultimately, policy-making must be guided by both data and (5)______ values.

t: Read the passage below and choose the correct word for each blank.
q.e: In the given context, a government prioritizing public welfare should be receptive to evaluation and feedback. "Criticism," along with citizen feedback, represents constructive input that helps improve governance, making it the most appropriate choice for blank (1).

The sentence emphasizes that proper coordination and timely communication between departments are fundamentally necessary to achieve successful outcomes. Therefore, "essential," meaning absolutely necessary or extremely important, is the most appropriate word for blank (2).

The context discusses how public awareness and access to accurate information enhance transparency. This openness directly helps in curbing or reducing dishonest conduct, making "corruption" the most contextually appropriate word for blank (3).

Digital platforms and e-governance tools are designed to facilitate civic engagement and boost citizen involvement. Therefore, the verb "increase," meaning to make greater in size or amount, correctly fits blank (4) in relation to public participation.

The sentence discusses guiding principles for policy-making in good governance. Policies should be driven by objective data and moral principles. Thus, "ethical," which relates to moral principles and integrity, is the most suitable adjective for blank (5).

p: The rapid adoption of digital tools has revolutionized the field of education. Online platforms, interactive modules, and virtual classrooms have made learning more accessible and (1)______ for students around the world. These technologies allow learners to progress at their own pace, revisit difficult concepts, and explore subjects beyond traditional syllabi. However, digital learning also brings certain challenges. Not all students have equal access to reliable internet or digital (2)______, which creates a significant learning gap. Moreover, prolonged screen time and lack of real-world interaction can affect both physical health and social development. To address these issues, institutions must adopt a blended approach — one that combines the flexibility of digital content with the structure of face-to-face learning. Teachers must also be trained to effectively integrate technology into the classroom, ensuring that it enhances rather than (3)______ the learning process. When used responsibly, digital education has the potential to (4)______ barriers and bring quality instruction to even the most remote corners of the world. But for it to be truly effective, students must stay disciplined, motivated, and (5)______ in their learning journey. (1)

q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: डिजिटल टूल्स ने शिक्षा को छात्रों की गति के अनुसार (at their own pace) बना दिया है, जिससे यह अधिक "व्यक्तिगत" (personalized) हो गई है।
Detailed Grammar/Explanation: चुनौती यह है कि हर छात्र के पास अच्छी इंटरनेट सुविधा या डिजिटल "उपकरण" (devices जैसे फोन/लैपटॉप) नहीं हैं।

Detailed Grammar/Explanation: शिक्षकों को तकनीक ऐसे इस्तेमाल करनी चाहिए कि वह पढ़ाई को बेहतर बनाए (enhances), न कि पढ़ाई में "बाधा डाले" (disrupts)। 'Enhances' का विपरीत 'disrupts' यहाँ बिल्कुल सही है।
Detailed Grammar/Explanation: अगर ज़िम्मेदारी से इस्तेमाल हो, तो डिजिटल शिक्षा दुनिया की तमाम रुकावटों या दीवारों को "तोड़ने" (break barriers) की क्षमता रखती है।
Detailed Grammar/Explanation: शिक्षा को प्रभावी बनाने के लिए छात्रों को अनुशासित, प्रेरित और पूरी तरह से "ध्यान केंद्रित" (focused) रहना चाहिए।

p: Aeroplane mode is a built-in smartphone feature that

(1) _____ all cellular, wireless, and Bluetooth signals. When passengers leave their cellular devices active during air travel, these devices continuously scan for network connections at full intensity. This intense scanning emits strong electromagnetic interference that can (2) _____ the aircraft's critical communication and navigation systems. Pilots frequently report hearing a distinct buzzing sound in their headsets. This sound may affect the clarity of communication during (3) _____ flight phases, when pilots rely heavily on instructions from the ground support team. These sounds can mask urgent radio commands from air traffic control. Moreover, cumulative signals from dozens of active devices can compromise the accuracy of flight deck instruments, such as altimeters and radar. While modern aircraft are engineered with advanced (4) _____, the potential for technology to fail under unexpected signal interference remains a reality. Compliance with aeroplane mode is not something to be taken lightly by the passengers. It is a vital safety (5) _____ that ensures pilots maintain a clear, uninterrupted line of communication with ground support, ensuring a safe journey for everyone on board.

t: In the following question,some of the words in the passage have been left out.Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
What should come in blank 1?
q.e: The fundamental purpose of aeroplane mode is to halt or shut off cellular communication. Therefore, "Disconnects" is the correct verb, as the feature actively cuts off or suspends all wireless and Bluetooth signals.

t: In the following question,some of the words in the passage have been left out.Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
What should come in blank 2?
q.e: Electromagnetic interference causes problems and breaks the operational flow of technology. Thus, the interference can "disrupt" (interrupt by causing a disturbance or problem) the aircraft's critical communication systems.

t: In the following question,some of the words in the passage have been left out.Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
What should come in blank 3?
q.e: The passage notes that pilots rely heavily on these instructions and mentions "urgent radio commands." Consequently, the flight phases being discussed are "crucial" (extremely important or decisive), rather than trivial or leisurely.

t: In the following question,some of the words in the passage have been left out.Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
What should come in blank 4?
q.e: To protect flight deck instruments from unexpected electromagnetic interference, aircraft are engineered with protective barriers. The technical and appropriate term for this protective engineering is "shielding."

t: In the following question,some of the words in the passage have been left out.Read the passage carefully and choose the correct answer to each question out of the four alternatives and fill in the blanks.
What should come in blank 5?
q.e: The act of turning on aeroplane mode is an established rule or standard procedure meant to maintain aviation safety. A formal rule of behavior or procedure like this is best defined as a "protocol."

p: The recent breakthroughs in CRISPR-Cas9 technology have moved the prospect of human genetic enhancement from the realm of science fiction into the laboratory. As researchers refine the precision of these "molecular scissors," the medical community finds itself at a (A)______. While the primary goal of such technology is to eradicate hereditary diseases, the potential for non-therapeutic modifications, such as altering physical traits or cognitive abilities, has (B)______ a global debate. If these tools are to be used ethically, international regulatory bodies must first establish a consensus on where "healing" ends and "enhancement" (C)______. Notwithstanding the immense therapeutic potential, many bioethicists remain wary of the long-term consequences. The human genome is a delicately balanced system, and there is a significant risk of "off-target" effects, where unintended parts of the DNAare altered. Such errors could result in new, unforeseen health complications that (D)______ not manifest until years later. Consequently, clinical trials are being conducted under rigorous oversight, ensuring that every procedure is subjected (E)______ the highest safety standards before it can be approved for widespread use.

t: Choose the correct word to fill in the blank (A) and complete the idiom:

p: Climate discourse, once the domain of ecological alarm and policy whitepapers, has now become a theater of geopolitical choreography. The carbon footprint becomes a moral metric only when traced in Southern sand; in Northern snow, it is reframed as "developmental necessity." Funding mechanisms are not immune to this dissonance. Green finance flows in tributaries engineered by creditworthiness, not climate need. Adaptation becomes a (2) _____, where vulnerable nations perform resilience to attract capital, rather than receive redress. "Net zero," meanwhile, floats like a talisman-invoked often, defined rarely. In such a paradigm, technocratic optimism obscures the uneven cartography of suffering. Satellites scan deforested zones with precision, but remain blind to the (3) _____ histories beneath them. Carbon markets, too, offer the illusion of absolution-one entity's excess "offset" by another's austerity. But offsets do not erase the heat; they only relocate the guilt. To resist climate colonialism is to unmask the benevolence of treaties and question the neutrality of metrics. Until the grammar of environmental justice is (4) _____, and not merely adjusted, any climate action risks becoming a ritual of (5) _____, not repair.

p: Bread, often hailed as the "staff of life," manifests in a myriad of forms across global cultures, each variety embodying unique ingredients, preparation methods, and historical significance. Leavened breads, (3) utilize yeast or other fermenting agents, are prized for their porous texture and complex flavours resulting from fermentation. Conversely, unleavened breads, such as tortillas and matzo, (1) eschew rising agents, offering a denser, flatter alternative often associated with religious or ceremonial contexts. The choice of flour wheat, rye, barley, or corn. Further diversifies bread's texture and taste profile. Artisanal bread making (4) a renaissance, with bakers emphasizing natural fermentation processes, organic ingredients, and traditional craftsmanship. This movement challenges the ubiquity of mass-produced loaves, which often contain preservatives and additives to extend shelf life but may compromise nutritional value and flavour. Bread's cultural resonance transcends sustenance; it symbolizes community, ritual, and identity. Whether breaking fast during Ramadan with pita or sharing challah during Shabbat, bread is integral to social and spiritual practices worldwide. Understanding these diverse types fosters appreciation of bread's role beyond mere nourishment, illuminating its place in human heritage (5) gastronomy.

p: Phenomenology suggests that time is not a series of discrete, ticking moments but a continuous, indivisible flow of consciousness. (A)______, our consciousness "protends" and "retains", pulling the past and the future into every single instant of awareness. Our perception of a "now" is constantly (B)______ by our memories of what has just occurred and our anticipations of what is about to happen. When you listen to a melody, you don't hear isolated notes; you hear the relationship between the note playing now and the ones that preceded it. The "now" is always pregnant with the "next". Were we to experience a moment in total isolation, stripped of all context and memory, it (C)______ to have any human meaning. It would be a "flash" without a narrative, a sensation without a self. Our very identity is built upon the temporal continuity that phenomenology seeks to describe and analyse. While objective clocks measure seconds with mechanical precision, the "lived time" of the individual is notoriously elastic. An hour spent in a state of flow can feel like minutes, while a minute of intense physical pain can feel like an eternity. The clock is a social (D)______; the experience of duration is a biological and psychological reality. This subjective stretching of duration is what makes a moment of joy feel fleeting and a moment of dread feel interminable. We are not mere observers of time; we are the medium (E)______ which time gains its quality. To understand the human condition, we must look beyond the stopwatch and into the shifting currents of internal experience.

p: In contrast to earthquakes or wars, other violence is insidious, playing itself out over decades smog, poisoned water, eroded soil. These are not shocks but creeping disasters. Such damage has been described as "slow violence," not because it is less profound, but because it is less spectacular. It does not have the dramatic images that grab the public eye. It is therefore frequently (1) _____ in media reporting, policy action, and public debate. This invisibility is not an accident. They present agony as the byproduct of progress or a technical glitch and not as systemic neglect. Agony is reported to victims as having no connection, their contexts misinterpreted. It hurts most those who have the least political power-rural poor, indigenous peoples, urban minorities. The privileged will never lay eyes on the toxins, but the marginalized inhale them. Without so much as a mention of this violence, resistance will continue to be fragmented and justice delayed. It takes more than policy to solve it -it takes a new kind of attention: slow noticing, slow journalism, slow solidarity. These are not positions of passivity but radical acts of care. They (3) _____ the rhythms of harm and provide room for grief, witness, and repair. Most legal systems are, however, constructed to address the spectacular, rather than the smoldering. p: Somewhere between the glint of touchscreen interfaces and the blur of algorithmic suggestion lies a silent erosion of pause. Regulation, in this context, is not merely about protection; it is about preserving (3)_____ in a system that privileges momentum over mindfulness. We do not need more personalization — we need more interruption. Only by interrupting the velocity of interface can we hope to return to the interiority that once defined being. p: Oceanic literature has long been obscured by Western perspectives that view the sea as a vast, empty void between "significant" landmasses. This shift in perspective transforms the ocean from a site of transit into a site of profound cultural belonging and identity. Had the early colonial cartographers respected the indigenous seafaring traditions and navigational charts, the maps of today might look very different. Instead of vast blue expanses labelled as "unexplored", we would see a web of ancestral pathways. The refusal to acknowledge these traditions was a deliberate act of (C)_____ silencing that facilitated colonial expansion. Though these narratives are often marginalised in global literary curricula, they provide a vital counter-history antithetical (D)_____ the standard tales of discovery. Their prose is often (E)_____ with metaphors of fluidity and currents, challenging the rigid, static borders imposed by imperial powers. This literature does not just tell a story; it performs an act of decolonisation. It reminds us that for those who call the ocean home, the water is the most solid ground they know.

p: To speak of the political as an abstract structure is, perhaps, already to concede to the logic of the archive: that which preserves through containment, and [1] _____ through its very naming. Resistance, if it resists at all, cannot be found in opposition, but in [2] _____ -in the refusal to be coherent, in the grammarless whisper. The body, meanwhile, becomes a ledger: inscribed, decoded, re-encoded. What justice can exist in such a system? Not that of law, but of rupture. A justice that unbinds, that refuses the terms of its own invocation. It is not reparation that is sought, but [3] _____ -the unworking of systems, the destitution of legibility. To enter this mode is to abandon appeal, to relinquish the comfort of meaning. One must instead submit to the possibility of a justice that never arrives, that remains [4] _____ excessive and unlocatable. Only then can we imagine a politics not of representation, but of presence without capture, of subjectivity without scaffolding. p: Equity in education is not a matter of distributing identical tools to unequal lives. It is, instead, the (1)_____ of design — one that begins by listening, not prescribing. p: The old lighthouse had stood on the jagged cliffs of Blackwood Bay for over a century, its lantern room long since emptied of its rotating flame. To the townsfolk below, the structure was a relic of a bygone era, yet for Elias, the retired keeper, it remained the only place where the world felt coherent. He spent his afternoons in the small circular room atop the spiral stairs, (A)______ the rhythmic crashing of the Atlantic against the rocks below. He often wondered about the rapidly changing modern world. Today's sailors did not need his guidance. They relied on satellite pings and digital charts, (B)______ their predecessors had eagerly looked for the steady, reassuring blink of his beacon to navigate the treacherous waters. There was a certain coldness to the new technology, a lack of human connection that Elias found difficult to (C)______. He believed that a machine could tell you where you were, but it could never tell you that you were safe. One evening, a storm of unprecedented ferocity swept in from the north, knocking out the town's power grid and plunging the bay into total darkness. In the sudden silence of the digital age, the people felt a (D)______ fear they had long-forgotten. Elias reached into his heavy oak cabinet and pulled out a rusted iron key. He knew that the emergency oil lamps were still in the cellar. As he struck a match and the first spark caught, the golden glow reflected in his eyes. For the panicking residents of the tiny coastal town, the flickering light wasn't a sign of outdated tech, but a beacon (E)______ hope.

t: Choose the grammatically correct option to fill in the blank (A).
q.e: The present participle phrase describes an ongoing accompanying action of spending afternoons. The verb "listen" requires the preposition "to" when taking an object ("the rhythmic crashing"). Therefore, "listening to" correctly completes the clause.

t: Fill in the blank (B) with the correct conjunction to fit the context.
q.e: The conjunction "whereas" is used to contrast two related facts. Here, it contrasts modern sailors who rely on satellite charts with past sailors who depended on the beacon light, making "whereas" the appropriate choice.

t: Fill in the blank (C) with the correct word to complete the idiom:
q.e: The idiom "to stomach something" means to tolerate, endure, or accept something unpleasant. In this context, Elias found the lack of human connection in modern technology difficult to accept, making "stomach" the correct choice.

t: Fill in the blank (D) with the word that means "original":
q.e: The word "primal" relates to an early, original, or instinctive evolutionary stage. In the given sentence, "primal fear" describes an instinctive, deeply rooted, and original dread brought back by the complete darkness and silence.

t: Choose the correct preposition to fill in the blank (E) to complete the fixed idiomatic expression:
q.e: The expression "a beacon of hope" is a standard fixed idiomatic phrase that refers to a person or thing that offers encouragement, guidance, or optimism during difficult circumstances. Therefore, the preposition "of" completes the idiom correctly.

p: I was strolling through the park one night when I saw a man sitting by himself on a bench. He was dressed in frayed clothes, and his face was creased with (1) ___. He looked lost in thought, gazing at the ground as if trying to find answers. I paused for a moment before going over to talk to him. When I said hello, he looked up and smiled weakly. He began talking to me about his life, including his triumphs and setbacks, love and grief. His stories were so enlightening, and his perspective (2) ___. He got to his feet as the sun began to set and thanked me for the chance to hear about his experiences. "Sometimes, all we need is someone to hear us," he stated. His words lingered in my mind, bringing to mind the (3) ___ of human connection. That night, I left the park humbled and (4) ___. Life is full of unexpected encounters, each one with the power to (5) ___ us in ways that we never thought possible.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 1?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The man is described as wearing frayed clothes, looking lost in thought, and gazing at the ground seeking answers. "Creased with worry" is a common idiom describing facial lines caused by chronic anxiety, which fits the somber description. Hindi Meaning: चिंता.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 2?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: His stories were described as "enlightening." The corresponding effect on the narrator's perspective is best captured by "enlightened," meaning it broadened and illuminated their worldview. Hindi Meaning: प्रबुद्ध / ज्ञान से भरा.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 3?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The man's statement, "Sometimes, all we need is someone to hear us," emphasizes the profound strength and impact of simply listening. This realization evokes "the power of human connection." Hindi Meaning: शक्ति / प्रभाव.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 4?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Humbled and inspired" is a natural pairing of emotions following a deeply meaningful and uplifting encounter. The narrator feels both a sense of modesty and a surge of motivation. Hindi Meaning: प्रेरित.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 5?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: The passage concludes with the realization that unexpected encounters can profoundly shape us. Given that the narrator felt "inspired" (from blank 4), the consistent theme is that such encounters hold the power to "inspire" positive growth. Hindi Meaning: प्रेरित करना.

p: Ravi and Arjun had been rivals on the football field since their first year in school. Both were talented players, and their competition often brought out the best and sometimes the worst-in them. When the school team was selected for the district championship, both were chosen to play. At first, their rivalry made teamwork difficult. Passes were missed, tempers (1) _____ and the coach had to step in. He reminded them that personal pride should never come before the team. Slowly, Ravi and Arjun began to (2) _____ one another's strengths instead of focusing on their differences. As trust grew, their coordination improved, and the team's performance soared. In the semi-final match, it was a pass from Ravi that helped Arjun score the winning goal. The crowd cheered not just for the win, but for the sportsmanship. What began as a clash ended in a strong (3) _____ that taught them the value of unity, mutual (4) _____ and shared (5) _____.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 1?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: "Tempers flared" एक प्रसिद्ध अंग्रेज़ी मुहावरा (Idiom) है जिसका अर्थ होता है 'अचानक गुस्सा भड़क उठना'। पास मिस होने के कारण दोनों को गुस्सा आ गया था। Hindi Meaning: (गुस्सा) भड़क उठना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 2?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: झगड़े के बाद, उन्होंने अपनी कमियों को देखने के बजाय एक-दूसरे की ताकतों (strengths) की "सराहना" (appreciate) करना शुरू कर दिया। Hindi Meaning: सराहना करना / कद्र करना.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 3?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: जो चीज़ एक 'टकराव' (clash) के रूप में शुरू हुई थी, वह अंततः एक मज़बूत "साझेदारी" (partnership) में बदल गई। Hindi Meaning: साझेदारी.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 4?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: 'Mutual respect' (आपसी सम्मान) टीमवर्क और अच्छे खेल (sportsmanship) की सबसे बड़ी नींव होती है। Hindi Meaning: सम्मान / आदर.

t: What should come in the place of blank number 5?
q.e: Detailed Grammar/Explanation: शुरुआत में उनके पास 'व्यक्तिगत अहंकार' (personal pride) था, लेकिन साथ खेलने के बाद उन्होंने "साझा गर्व" (shared pride) का मूल्य सीखा, यानी अब वे अकेले नहीं, बल्कि पूरी टीम की जीत पर गर्व करते हैं। Hindi Meaning: गर्व.

p: The REM (Rapid Eye Movement) cycle is a sleep stage (1) _____ by rapid eye movements, low muscle tone throughout the body, and vivid dreaming. It gets its name because our eyes rapidly dart back and forth behind our closed eyelids, signalling (3) _____ brain activity. To protect us from physically acting out these wild dreams and hurting ourselves, our brain temporarily (4) _____ our major muscles. This temporary lockdown is called muscle atonia. Neurologists view the REM cycle as the brain's ultimate overnight cleanup crew; it (5) _____ our daily emotions, sharpens our memory, and stores everything we learned during the day.
